summary: t_i = ∑_l (∑_v r_{v,i}X_{v,c})^{p^{2l}} up to terms of high order, so ∑_i t_i^p r_{x,i} = ∑_{l,v} (∑_i r_{v,i}^{p^{2l+1}} r_{x,i})·X_{(v,c)}^{p^{2l+1}}; distinct (l, v) give distinct monomials.

steps.claim: p > 1, and the power series ring has characteristic p.

Write t_i = ∑_{l} (∑_v r_{v,i}X_{(v,c)})^{p^{2l}} plus a series of order > deg d (`eq_sum_pow_of_sub_pow_eq` with B = deg d; the remainder has nilpotent constant term and high order); raising to the p-th power (additive in characteristic p) and multiplying by r_{x,i}: the coefficient of d in ∑_i t_i^p r_{x,i} is the sum over (l, v) with d = p^{2l+1}·e_{(v,c)} of ∑_i r_{v,i}^{p^{2l+1}}r_{x,i}.
steps.lean:
simp (disch := grind [Nat.lt_pow_self]) [congrArg (· ^ p) (eq_sum_pow_of_sub_pow_eq (ht _)
    d.degree), add_pow_char, ← pow_mul, ← pow_succ, ← smul_eq_C_mul, sum_mul, @sum_comm _ _ J,
    coeff_X_pow, coeff_eq_zero_of_constantCoeff_nilpotent (m := 1), ← sum_product']

steps.claim: Both directions: a nonzero coefficient comes from some (n, y) with nonzero sum; conversely at d = p^{2n+1}e_{(y,c)} only the term (n, y) contributes (p^a = p^b ⟹ a = b; single exponents are equal only for equal variables and degrees).
steps.lean:
